target_customer: Distributed teams and small groups needing browser based real time conferencing and collaboration
problem: Remote groups needed to meet and work together online without installing software; Team Apart offered real time group collaboration in the browser.
business_model: Not stated in sources; likely subscription collaboration software but unconfirmed
product_category: Real time online collaboration and web conferencing

founders.name: Wes Hather
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page bio, which also lists Techstars Summer 2011 and YC Summer 2008.

founders.name: Michael Hoisie
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no bio. The directory team size is 2 while three founders are listed.

competitors.name: Dimdim
competitors.what: Browser based web conferencing with no download for attendees, pitched as a WebEx alternative
competitors.traction_then: Reported more than 500,000 users in early 2008

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time browser collaboration in 2008 without plugins needed custom streaming and synchronization, which was hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Established web conferencing products and open source Dimdim covered the same need and a collaboration tool had no data or network lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer found. Dimdim, a rival, was bought by Salesforce for 31 million dollars in January 2011.

market_need_then: Web conferencing demand was visible in 2008 as Dimdim reported fast user growth, but nothing shows Team Apart's own traction.

branding.domain_note: teamapart.com did not resolve from the research environment (fetch failed), so the domain is treated as dead or unreachable.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, community or assets found beyond the YC directory entry.

outcome_analysis: Team Apart was a Summer 2008 YC company building real time browser based group collaboration, a space already served by Dimdim and larger conferencing vendors. No shutdown announcement, post mortem, funding round or traction figure is public, so the cause of its inactive status is not public and no failure factors are asserted. The founders went on to start Outreach.io and Spot.
notes: CB Insights lists Y Combinator as an investor with an unattributed round and no amount or date; no round is recorded. Search for outcome, funding and branding returned only the YC page. Dimdim is dated April 2008 (hosted launch), which predates the batch end. Whether Team Apart actually competed head to head with Dimdim is inferred from the product category in the YC and CB Insights descriptions.
